title: Occlusal fit of posterior crowns based on a digital manufacturing process with AI-based functional analysis vs. with known mean values: a prospective, randomized clinical study
summary: A prospective clinical study with 18 patients receiving single crowns. The aim is to prove that the use of artificial intelligence-based functional analysis with Bite-Finder Software (BFS) can be used to produce accurately fitting crowns and thus minimize surface preparation by grinding. After preparation of the tooth or after insertion of the abutment in the case of implant crowns, intraoral upper and lower jaw scans are taken.  The scans are then matched and the dental technician uses the generated data to produce two crowns.  One crown according to the already known conventional mean values and a second crown according to the digitally and individually determined values. The crowns are then adjusted. The interfering contacts can be detected with occlusal foil and then ground in until the crown fits and can be definitively fixed; the time required for this is recorded.  The crowns are scanned before and after milling to measure the amount of material milled from the occlusal surface with BFS. The practitioner will select and cement the more optimal crown from the two crowns produced.
conditions: Loss of teeth due to accident, extraction or local periodontal disease

interventions.name: Crown produced with the Bite-Finder software.
Crown produced according to known conventional mean values.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- At least 18 years of age 
- On a voluntary basis /Signed declaration of consent to participate in the study 
- Clinically confirmed that a dental crown is required in the posterior region.
Exclusion criteria:
- Periodontal therapy necessary or not completed
- Abutment situations that do not allow a scan (e.g. deep subgingival preparation).
- Pregnant patients.
